problem: Existing VLN-CE cross-modal planning policies are studied independently: map-based policies (graph grounding) are strong at spatial reasoning but weak at procedural alignment, while route-based policies (sequential observation-instruction alignment) are the reverse, so agents relying on one ability plan poorly in complex scenes.
motivation: Effective VLN-CE needs both spatial reasoning to explore toward the target under partial observability and procedural alignment to follow the instruction sequence. Inspired by human navigation, which uses both a cognitive map and route knowledge, the paper combines the two policy types.
key_idea: Build a multiplex spatio-procedural topological graph and run map-based and route-based policies in parallel, fusing them by feature-level collaboration and logit-level fusion.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The claim is that the two policy types are complementary, and that integrating them at both the feature and logit levels beats using either alone.
method: Spatio-Procedural Topological Mapping: constructs a multiplex graph that supports learning both map-based and route-based policies.
Dual-Stream Encoding: performs cross-modal encoding of instruction and graph for both policies in parallel.
Hierarchical Policy Integration: fuses the two policies via feature-level collaboration and logit-level fusion.
